      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering",
      "body": "The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering AuditLogEntry by '-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, self.key))) and value_from_cursor returns a raw integer. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so math.floor/ceil raises TypeError on the first non-empty result page, and an integer cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column. The result is that any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true that returns audit logs fails with a 500 error."

      "title": "Negative offset slicing is not supported by Django querysets",
      "body": "OptimizedCursorPaginator's advanced path sets start_offset to cursor.offset when cursor.offset is negative and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor offsets come from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indexes with AssertionError, so a cursor such as 0:-1:1 can cause an unhandled 500. The inline comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect."
    },

      "title": "BasePaginator also passes negative prev offsets to queryset slicing",
      "body": "BasePaginator.get_result was changed to clamp negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false. When is_prev is true, a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Because Cursor.from_string parses negative integers, any BasePaginator-based endpoint, including the default DateTimePaginator path for audit logs, can be made to crash by a client-supplied previous cursor with a negative offset."

The queryset ordering is therefore left unchanged, so backward pagination over a queryset already ordered descending can use the wrong sort direction and return incorrect pages or cursors."

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering
findings.body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering AuditLogEntry by '-datetime'. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(getattr(item, self.key))) and value_from_cursor returns a raw integer. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so math.floor/ceil raises TypeError on the first non-empty result page, and an integer cursor value would also be compared to a timestamp column. The result is that any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true that returns audit logs fails with a 500 error.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing is not supported by Django querysets
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator's advanced path sets start_offset to cursor.offset when cursor.offset is negative and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Cursor offsets come from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indexes with AssertionError, so a cursor such as 0:-1:1 can cause an unhandled 500. The inline comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect.

findings.title: BasePaginator also passes negative prev offsets to queryset slicing
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed to clamp negative offsets only when cursor.is_prev is false. When is_prev is true, a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Because Cursor.from_string parses negative integers, any BasePaginator-based endpoint, including the default DateTimePaginator path for audit logs, can be made to crash by a client-supplied previous cursor with a negative offset.

findings.title: Typo assigns to query_b instead of order_by
findings.body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, the branch that flips an existing '-key' ordering to ascending assigns tuple(new_order_by) to queryset.query_b instead of queryset.query.order_by. The queryset ordering is therefore left unchanged, so backward pagination over a queryset already ordered descending can use the wrong sort direction and return incorrect pages or cursors.

findings.title: No tests for the new pagination toggle or OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: The PR adds a query-parameter-gated paginator, an admin-only advanced feature, and negative-offset handling, but includes no tests for the new endpoint behavior, cursor parsing, forward/backward pagination, or invalid/negative cursors. Given the runtime crashes with datetime fields and negative offsets, this is a high-risk untested change.
